comparator.name: American Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026 intake takes 60 EC each year. Year two includes four rotating Special Topics courses. Year three includes a 30 EC minor or approved study abroad, a research seminar, a faculty-wide course and a thesis.

questionsApplications.label: How has American history shaped present identities, inequalities and social conflicts?
How do democratic institutions, political texts, movements and rhetoric shape American power?
How do literature, media and popular culture create and contest ideas of America?
How do migration, capitalism, globalisation and regional difference connect the Americas to the wider world?

alternatives.concept: Explore how U.S. history, democratic institutions and popular culture shape American society. Study gender and Indigenous histories, compare political systems, and investigate race and representation through media, literature and historical research.

alternatives.concept: Explore how film, media, literature and art tell stories about American life. Begin with narrative and film analysis, study race and representation in American media, then use adaptation, documentary and creative work to examine how cultural meaning is made.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest match is complemented by two feasible generator-backed directions: American literature, media and cultural expression; and American politics, identity and global affairs. Each has a different organising logic, produces material curricular consequences and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC floor, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached. The separately assessed hemispheric migration and political-economy direction is not feasible as a 24-course Americas-focused programme because UCR lacks a sufficient regional sequence in Canada, Latin America and religion in the Americas; general global, economic and migration courses would not reproduce that target-specific direction.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Groningen continues its dedicated Americas survey. UCR’s Modern History provides wider historical context.
Both examine modern U.S. history. Histories of Gender focuses on gender, slavery and lived experience.
Both examine Indigenous histories and colonization. Native American Histories follows these themes beyond the early republic.
Groningen requires a thesis. UCR’s historical research course culminates in a paper, and optional independent research is shown separately.
Both examine political institutions, parties and democratic participation. UCR compares political systems across countries.
Groningen studies political and media theory together. UCR studies contemporary social theory and media in separate courses.
Both guide students through a sustained research project. The UCR course focuses on historical inquiry and source criticism.
Groningen examines how stories shape identities. UCR offers related literary and media analysis.
Groningen compares societies and cultures across the Americas. UCR offers related work in history, politics and literary interpretation.
Choose a faculty-wide course in one of the published themes.
Both develop written and spoken argument. UCR emphasizes rhetoric and audience.
This course continues Groningen’s introduction to cultural theory.
Groningen introduces cultural analysis of race, class and gender. UCR explores these themes through sociology and history.
Both develop independent research through question design and analysis. UCR focuses on qualitative social research.
